title: Library

topics.title: Library location

topics.title: Library timings
topics.answer: Monday to Saturday, 8:30 AM to 8:00 PM. The reading hall stays open up to 10:00 PM during mid-semester and end-semester examinations.

topics.title: Library rules
topics.answer:
From the official CGC Library Rules PDF:
**Card:** every student needs a stamp-size photograph for the identity-cum-library card. It is non-transferable, must be carried in the library and college, and shown when staff ask. Report a lost card at once so the membership can be blocked.
**Borrowing:** graduate and postgraduate students can issue 3 books for 21 days. A fine is charged for late return.
**Reference books and magazines** can only be read inside the library.
**Belongings:** bags, personal items and books from other libraries must be left at the property counter. The library is not responsible for them. Show your files and books to the staff at the check-point when leaving.
**Conduct:** no eating, sleeping or smoking. Keep silence and switch off mobile phones.
**Care of books:** do not write on, mark or tear books. Borrowers are responsible for damage, so report existing damage before issue.
**Lost book:** tell the librarian and replace it or pay its price within a week of the due date. The late fine continues until it is settled.
After reading, leave books on the table and do not shelve them. Ask the staff if you cannot find something.

topics.title: How to issue a book
topics.answer: To borrow books you need your identity-cum-library card (it cannot be shared with anyone). Graduate and postgraduate students can issue 3 books for 21 days. Reference books and magazines are for use inside the library only, and bags must be left at the property counter. The exact steps at the issue counter are not in the rules PDF: Information not available yet.

topics.title: How to return a book
topics.answer: Return books on or before the due date (21 days after issue). A fine is charged for late return; the PDF does not state the amount. If a book is lost, tell the librarian and replace it or pay its price within a week of the due date. After reading in the library, leave books on the table. The renewal procedure: Information not available yet.
topics.unconfirmed: Older stored data mentions a late fine of Rs. 2 per day per book and renewal on or before the due date.

topics.title: How many books can I issue
topics.answer: Graduate and postgraduate students can issue 3 books for 21 days (official Library Rules). Limits for faculty or staff: Information not available yet.
topics.unconfirmed: The help-desk data adds 'extra books for meritorious/SC students'. This is not in the official PDF text.

topics.title: Library facilities
topics.answer: Per the official library page: the library is fully automated with LIBSYS software, monitored by CCTV, and has over 1.25 lakh books on open shelves, plus CDs, e-books, journals and e-journals.
topics.unconfirmed:
A subsidised Book Bank scheme for prescribed textbooks, and air-conditioned reading halls for 500+ students with Wi-Fi.

Help-desk data: the CCT library has 9495+ volumes and 1217+ titles; the CGC group libraries about 1.21 lakh+ volumes (the official page says over 1.25 lakh). Software: LIBSYS catalogue and Turnitin plagiarism checking.

topics.title: Digital library
topics.answer: The library subscribes to e-books and e-journals usable anytime, anywhere. The official guide is the Digi Library PDF. Login details are not published.
topics.unconfirmed:
Online Public Access Catalogue (OPAC): Fully automated with Koha/ERP software allowing students to search book availability, author, title, and shelf location from any campus terminal or mobile portal.
Subscribed Databases: IEEE Xplore Digital Library, ScienceDirect/Elsevier, SpringerLink, J-Gate, and EBSCOhost for engineering, management, and pharmacy research papers.
National Resource Networks: Institutional Member of DELNET (Developing Library Network) enabling Inter-Library Loan (ILL) and document delivery across 5,000+ partner libraries.
National Digital Library of India (NDLI): Registered NDLI Institutional Club member providing free access to 60+ million digital learning resources, video lectures, and rare manuscripts.
E-Newspapers & Magazines: Economic Times, The Hindu, Indian Express, Business Standard, PCQuest, and Harvard Business Review accessible in the digital reading section.

Help-desk data: EBSCO e-books (2.49 lakh+), National Digital Library (45 lakh+), DELNET and EBSCO e-journals.
